title: Merriam-Webster Dictionary Adds 1,400 New Words
paragraphs: The American dictionary publisher Merriam-Webster has added about 1,400 new words and definitions to its online dictionary.
The update, announced in September 2026, includes words from a wide range of areas, including internet slang, dating, artificial intelligence, food, music, and health and wellness.

Some of the new words come from social media and internet culture. "Glow-up," for example, is defined as a usually dramatic improvement, especially to someone's appearance. "Looksmaxxing," meaning trying to improve one's looks as much as possible, was also added, as was "Rickroll," which refers to tricking someone into clicking a link to a famous 1980s music video. Other additions include "crashout" and "copium."

Dating has also inspired new entries. "Cuffing season" describes the colder months of the year, when single people look for short-term romantic partners, and "promposal" describes an invitation to a school prom.

Technology is another major source of new words. "AGI," short for artificial general intelligence, and "vibe coding" were both added. The word "compute" is now also listed as a noun, meaning the computing power that a program needs to run.

Food lovers will recognize several additions, too, such as "superfood," "cake pop" and "chili crisp." Other new words include "Mandela effect," which describes a false memory shared by many people, "Sunday scaries," the anxiety some people feel as the weekend ends, and "trash panda," a humorous name for a raccoon.
Merriam-Webster said its new entries reflect words that have been widely used over time. According to the company, a word is not added simply because it is popular for a short time.
